answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by accepting only identities a national digital-ID issuer binds to one recorded biometric per human; duplicates are rejected. Extra identities need extra real humans with valid documents, each costing C, and a public randomness beacon selects credentials for re-verification unpredictably. Unlike a copper coin or yarrow stem, a credential is not shareable because the issuer compares biometrics, not tokens. Per-epoch reward R means n sybils earn n(R-C), so cloning pays only if R>C. Assumption: issuer enforces one-per-person; corrupt issuer is weakness.
